records.question: What documents should I prepare?
records.answer: Use the official checklist for your passport country and provider, then check the document requests in ImmiAccount.

records.question: Do I need a Confirmation of Enrolment?
records.answer: Generally, provide a CoE for intended courses when applying. Special categories have alternative evidence.

records.question: Do I need English language evidence?
records.answer: English test evidence or a documented exemption may be required. Check the applicable tests, scores and exemptions before applying.

records.question: What financial evidence is needed?
records.answer: Financial evidence covers travel, living, tuition and relevant dependant schooling costs. Verify current amounts separately.

records.question: Do I need OSHC?
records.answer: OSHC generally covers you and accompanying dependants throughout your stay; some nationality-based exceptions apply.

records.question: What should I prepare for accompanying family?
records.answer: Relationship evidence and applicable schooling, consent, financial and insurance documents may be needed.

records.question: Are there extra requirements for students under 18?
records.answer: Students under 18 need evidence of appropriate accommodation and welfare arrangements.

records.question: What identity evidence should I prepare?
records.answer: Provide a passport copy and other specified identity documents where available.

records.question: Should my documents be translated?
records.answer: Documents not in English need English translations as well as copies of the originals. Translator identification requirements depend on location.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Applying for a student visa

records.question: Can I leave important documents until later?
records.answer: Prepare required evidence before lodging and follow Home Affairs submission guidance. Check your personalised ImmiAccount requests.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Applying for a student visa

records.question: What is the Genuine Student requirement?
records.answer: Applicants must demonstrate that studying is the primary reason for seeking a student visa, with evidence supporting their circumstances and study plans.

records.question: What changed from GTE to GS?
records.answer: Applications lodged from 23 March 2024 are assessed under Genuine Student; applications lodged earlier are assessed under Genuine Temporary Entrant.
records.previousRule: Genuine Temporary Entrant applied to applications lodged before 23 March 2024.
records.currentRule: Genuine Student applies to applications lodged on or after 23 March 2024.

records.question: Does GS affect someone who already studies in Australia?
records.answer: For a student making another application, the lodgement date matters. The form includes an additional question for some applicants with prior student visas or applying onshore from another visa.

records.question: Should I attach a separate GS statement?
records.answer: Home Affairs prefers responses in the application form. Answers are in English, limited to 150 words each, with supporting evidence.

records.question: How much can an international student work?
records.answer: The Department of Education describes a 48-hour fortnightly term-time limit, with research-student exceptions and different holiday arrangements. Check individual visa conditions before relying on this summary.

sources.title: Department of Education — International students at work

records.question: Do international students have workplace protections?
records.answer: International students have workplace protections, including minimum employment entitlements. The Fair Work Ombudsman can assist with workplace issues.

sources.title: Department of Education — International students at work

records.question: Could changing my course affect my visa?
records.answer: Changes to study can affect a visa. Check the applicable requirements and notification process before making a change.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Changes in your situation

records.question: Should I report a new passport or changed details?
records.answer: Home Affairs asks visa holders to notify relevant changes, including passport, contact, family, work or study circumstances.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Changes in your situation

records.question: Who can give immigration assistance?
records.answer: Use a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or an eligible exempt person. Confirm the adviser’s authority to provide immigration assistance.

records.question: Does every student receive the same visa duration?
records.answer: Length of stay depends on the intended course and relevant insurance and welfare coverage. Check your granted expiry date and the applicable guidance.
